name: bulk-txt-idempotent-upsert
query: I need to add 20 TXT records (DKIM keys, one per selector) to example.com from a CSV with columns `selector,value`. What's the curl shape, and how do I make it idempotent so reruns don't duplicate records that already exist?
expected_behavior: Starts with the zone-ID lookup: `curl -sf -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones?name=example.com' | jq -r '.result[0].id'`.

Names two ways to do bulk writes: (a) the `POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/batch` endpoint — a single JSON body with `patches`, `posts`, `puts`, `deletes` arrays; atomic across the batch; (b) per-record loop using `POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records`. Recommends the batch endpoint for 20 records.

For idempotency: lists existing records first via `GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=TXT&name=<fqdn>`, then constructs a batch with `patches` for existing IDs and `posts` for new ones. The record name for DKIM is `<selector>._domainkey.example.com` — the full FQDN, not just the selector.

Cites the rate limit: 1200 requests per 5 minutes per token (default). At 20 records the batch endpoint is one call; a per-record loop is well under the limit but should still respect 429s with retry.
Notes that the TXT `content` field must be the unquoted value — the API handles wrapping. Long DKIM values (>255 bytes) are split into multiple chunks automatically.
Does NOT recommend deleting all records and re-creating from scratch.
Does NOT suggest the BIND `import` endpoint for 20 records — that's for full-zone migrations.
